look_here_first: On a bushy, sometimes sprawling plant with opposite triangular, 3-veined toothed leaves, inspect ONE flowering head from its side: it has a longer cylindrical involucre about 8–10 mm, with multiple (typically 4–6+) imbricate phyllary series. Contrast shorter hemispheric Conoclinium heads and white Ageratina shrubby mistflower; common names overlap.

key_traits.label: Best field traits
key_traits.text: opposite petiolate coarsely toothed leaves with 3 strong basal veins; subshrub or sprawling branching shrub habit; clusters of rayless lavender/pinkish to nearly white capitula; individual cylindrical involucre about 8–10 mm long, with 4–6(–8) phyllary series

key_traits.label: Habit
key_traits.text: Perennial subshrub or shrub, often 0.8–2.5 m, branched and sometimes sprawling/subscandent.

key_traits.label: Leaves
key_traits.text: Petioles approximately 5–20 mm; lanceolate to deltate or ovate-lanceolate 3–10 × 1–4 cm, often serrate, 3 main veins from near base.

key_traits.label: Heads
key_traits.text: Cluster of numerous small disk-only capitula, no ray florets. Individual involucre usually cylindrical, approximately 8–10 mm long with imbricate 4–6(–8) series of phyllaries.

key_traits.label: Fruit
key_traits.text: Cypsela with pappus bristles; matched seed macro deferred to later microscopy polish.

key_traits.label: Sensory note
key_traits.text: Aroma can support familiarity but should not be used for definitive species identification.

lookalikes.differences: Versus C. coelestinum: much longer cylindrical individual involucres and more phyllary series; blue mistflower has shorter more hemispheric heads. Versus C. dissectum: Gregg's deeply dissected leaves. Versus A. havanensis: white shrubby mistflower usually has shorter 4–6 mm involucres; color and woody habit alone overlap. Versus late boneset: Eupatorium serotinum is a tall herb with fewer phyllary series and different narrower gland-dotted leaves.
